Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Feedback

I find this SCP of particular interest in that it could potentially have serious implications for the foundation itself. Think about it. If it is a library that contains possibly every book that could ever exist, then it would stand to reason that somewhere inside the library lies the following:

Every possible SCP that ever exists.
Every complete explaination for every SCP that exists.
Every complete explaination for every SCP written in such a way that even the average layman can understand it perfectly.
The answer to what SCP-001 really is.
Which SCPs need to be contained and which ones can be safely released without any ill effects.
The complete history of the foundation to it's very beginnings.
And more.

But conversely while the truth behind every SCP can be found in 1986, so can every lie as well.

It is unbearable knowledge that somewhere in this place, the answers to all of the foundation's questions exist yet remains inaccessible. If only there was a way to determine which books would lead to these truths, we could finally provide humanity with some sense of security and control when exposed to these anomalies since they would be anomalies no more. But as far as we know, no such thing exists.

Such pondering could drive one to utter insanity.

item.title: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Urban Legend

Page Layout: Standard description, some interview

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a beaten backpack with UC, Santa Cruz, patches on it. Once opened the person opening it is slowly replaced, physically and mentally, with a young philosophy student who then returns to exploring the continental United States. He also writes about his experiences, which helps pay his way.

Central Narrative: In 1989 Charles Anton Page decided to drop out of college and explore America; he felt trapped and needed to run away. He quickly adopted a "one week at a time" philosophy, where he'd find odd jobs and beg in order to obtain enough to buy a bus ticket and some food, and then would take off on the next leg of his journey.

A year or so later, he was robbed and left for dead, and would eventually succumb to his wounds. The body was never recovered. His backpack, and the contents therein, were pawned at a local pawn shop. Someone bought the backpack, and over the next few hours was transformed into a virtual clone of Page, but without the knowledge of his death or that he was leading an extended life.

He is able to live for one week (168 hours) at a time before copies of the wounds that killed him appear on his body, and he then quickly succumbs to them. Once someone finds and opens the backpack, he is yet again allowed to live for another week, but with the usual memory lapse.

While he has adapted to the modern world somewhat (he writes a blog instead of magazine articles), he is still driven to explore the continental United States. He just does it one week at a time.

Hook/Attention Grabber: A basic urban legend about a youth cut short but still trying to find a way to accomplish his dream of exploring the United States through a mix of odd jobs, bus tickets, and hitchhiking, one week at a time.

item.title: Re: Elevator
item.content:encoded:
Heyo! I'll come and crit your draft you. Keep in mind I'm not clincal tone pro, so this'll largely be a 'what I think in general' type crit.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

SCP-XXXX is located at what was previously known as █████ Inc.

Generally, redacting/blackboxing something in the ConProcs (Special Containment Procedures) isn't a good idea. Realistically speaking, redacting information in the ConProcs doesn't make sense in-universe. These are the procedures—made as simple and basic as possible for personnel—for containing something. Redacting part of the information would just make the job more difficult than it needs to be.

Also, even out of ConProcs, I don't really see a reason to redact the name of a location. In universe, you're being granted clearance to read a classified article. Knowing where it came from usually isn't going to be that bad.

and administered Class A Amnestic.

Put 'a' between 'administered' and 'class'.

Following the unauthorized use of SCP-XXXX, no personnel under level four clearance are allowed in the same building as SCP-XXXX.

Probably a personal thing, but 'below level four clearance' sounds better than 'under'.

elevator shaft.The

Put a space between 'shaft.' and 'The'.

The elevator itself is comprised of steel and has seven buttons on the inside of it.

Remove 'itself'. Intuition says it's a tad unclinical to put it there.

SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator but when button seven is pressed the person(s) inside the elevator will be taken to the place they most desire to go.

'most desire to go' sounds off.
Let's try, 'SCP-XXXX functions as a normal elevator, but when the seventh button is pressed, the person(s) inside will be transported to a location they subconsciously desire.'

Inside is a GPS that records the places it has gone.

Let's try, 'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously traversed locations.'

The elevator will not work without it.

'The elevator will not function without the GPS.'
That said, I'm not sure how to feel about this line. I assume the GPS is just planted in the elevator. Also, this implies that the personnel have tried…removing it? I don't see why they'd do that.

Places recorded have been The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.

I think you can merge this with an earlier sentence to turn it into:
'Inside is a GPS that keeps records of previously explored locations, examples including The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England.'

It's cleaner and smoother.

In all instances the elevator returns within 20 minutes after leaving the facility area.

Puts a comma after 'instances'

Always talked of "the fields".

Hmmm you can change 'of' to 'about' and it would be better, but it still sounds unclinical.

Maybe, 'Frequently mentioned a location he referred to as, 'the fields.'

personnel.Camera feed was choppy but the surroundings were normal.

Space after 'personnel.'

You should bold out 'Dr. Spencer's Diary' whenever you write down the entries. It makes it stand out and look cleaner.

'Foundation' should be capitalized because it's a proper noun.

The elevators GPS showed the word unkown on the location.

'GPS displayed 'unknown' as the location.'

Results: D-7586 appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.

I don't really like the way this is worded. 'Appeared to have died of asphyxiation, presumably from being subjected to outer space.'

You could just say that D-7586 died from exposure to outer space. It's been stated plainly thus far that the elevator takes you to where you want to go.

'Presume: suppose that something is the case on the basis of probability.'

There really isn't much probability here.

Apologies if this part sounds kinda overly nitpicky.

D-4576 was a surfer. She lived on the beach and says that is where her heart is. D-4576 is very kind to all personnel considering the situation she is in.

Clinical tone is meant to portray something as emotionlessly as possible. This passage reads a little too much like normal prose.
We could change it to, 'D-4576 once had a significant interest in surfing. She lived on a beach prior to becoming D-Class. She has been cooperative thus far.'

Even then, I'm not sure mentioning the cooperative part is necessary. Unless she shown shown be to uncooperative beforehand.

When D-4576 arrived back at the facility she was covered in sand. She stated it was the best day she has had in forever. Her dopamine levels were extremely high.

Second sentence is too emotional. Adjectives like 'extremely' are usually non-clinical.

Test 4 reads…super awkwardly. As well as the diary entry beforehand.

Also, the reference to SCP-682 wasn't a good move because references/cross-links nowadays are frowned upon.

This was a strange piece to critique, considering this is a greenlit idea with a draft from over a year ago. I looked at the edit history and see that it was updated a few days ago, yes, but it still feels…strange. I'll detail this more in my final thoughts collapsible.

+Final Thoughts
-Final Thoughts

All in all, I'm not sure how to feel about this. 'Get in thing and go to desired/weird locale at push of button/drop of hat' isn't anything new, but it's always the execution that matters more than the concept. Everything has already been done in storytelling history, it's about what you do with a thing to differentiate it that makes it special.

But from what I've seen of your current draft, it's really standard with sub-clinical tone, bizarre and not really believable diary entries and a plot that essentially equates to 'these test logs freak me out and I'm afraid I might die. GG, fuck this.'

I should let you know that I, myself, am still pretty new here and I wasn't here in 2019; I joined a few months ago as of me writing this down. From what I've heard and seen, generic testing logs with little information aren't really good anymore.

I've heard one person say that testing logs aren't really good anymore, period, but like I think you could make this SCP work if you…say…

Did more in depth logs with video logs and such. Strap a video cam to some D-Class, have them go through some stuff and extend each test log to being a mini-adventure. Pretty standard stuff, but there's always an audience for that.

Also, you'll need to incorporate the researcher more organically into the story rather than have them write some extremely barebones diary entries.

Maybe they could maintain communication with the test D-Class subjects during test logs?

From what I've seen of your current logs, they essentially stick D-class in the thing, wave goodbye and tell them to be back before dinner. That doesn't really make sense considering the D-Class can just leave and not come back.

All in all, I hope everything I wrote made sense and I hope I helped. Good luck with this piece. I hope you continue pursuing this because it's nice to contribute to a lovely site like this ^_^

Forum thread: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France

+1 because it's a fun story as it is, but seconding all of SirPudding's comments above.1 This could be much, much stronger as both scifi and pulpy old-school horror with some tinkering.

For instance, on the technical side it's easier to get into orbit around Jupiter than around Mercury (short version is that Mercury doesn't help you brake), and the farther you get from the Sun - and to a lesser extent, planets - the better readings you're going to get from any sort of deep-space observatory. A station in solar orbit between Jupiter and Mars would be relatively easy to set up with the help of some lagrangian points, and put your station in empty space, any planets just distant points of light. (That's good for both observatories and for creep factor)

On the narrative side, I think a slower and more subtle buildup would amplify the creep factor exponentially. On this front, I could actually see some really interesting potential if you were to change it to be affecting the ground crew of a probe- say, they're operating the thing from an isolated antenna station in the middle of nowhere, and events gradually escalate from cafeteria discussions about weird signals and if anybody heard a dog barking last night, to security cam footage of a hallway door acting like someone opened an airlock.

Footnotes
1. With the exception that Dr. Weir in Event Horizon is artisan ham of the finest cut.

item.title: {Seeking Greenlight} The World's Best Pizza.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Comedy, Weirdness, short and sweet

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation stumbles upon a small family-owned restaurant that happens to serve infallibly, undeniably good food.

Central Narrative: After being flagged by CHORUS, A social mapping AIC designed to detect intense spikes in mood, a small pizzeria finds itself under the attention of the Foundation. The restaurant, known as Giacomo's Pizza, makes the pretty standard claim that it serves "The World's Best." The thing is, for this bistro, that might actually be true. Anyone who tries Giacomo's pies agrees that they're the best they ever tasted -or will taste- to the point of profound satisfaction. The thing is, the foundation can't figure out why. It's just normal pizza; nothing memetic, nothing thaumaturgic, nothing chemical. In the end, when the lead researcher breaks down to the current Giacomo in charge, tearfully asking them what's so special about their pizza they merely reply "Simple. They're made with love."
Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook of the article lies in the surrealist concept of an item of food being objectively "the best." As well as the intrigue of the eyecatching associated image:

Image block within
Close and return

Additional Notes:
While this article takes on a comedic tone, I do not intend it to be a -J. Many Skips turn funny concepts into sound articles, and I want this to be one of them.

item.title: Tale 1 of Tau-13
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre(s): Horror, Action

Page Layout: Given that this is a tale, I was going to write it like your standard narrative-driven novel. This is also the format I write most things in, save aspects of the SCP article I've drafted.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This first one will detail the team's first mission together, with flashbacks to their lives together in training.
  • The mission will involve them investigating a cult-like organization, who have been reportedly been kidnapping locals from a nearby town.
  • Upon investigation, they learn that the cult has been worshiping a horrible, Lovecraftian monster.
  • They, of course, go in for expulsion and containment.
  • They have a hard-fought battle, and through some stupid, neglectful mistakes, they lose their private to the monster.
  • Since they had all grown together in training and just as good friends, the sight of their private getting killed, combined with the psychic effects of the monstrosity, drive them very near to the edge of insanity.
  • After eventually routing out the cult, they return with broken minds. I'm thinking I'll have the Foundation use amnestics to make them forget the horrors, but deep down they still have that vastly stronger, Pavlovian-esque drive to protect each other and all innocents from these, and similar, horrors1.

Central Narrative: With the above in mind, the context is related to my SCP article currently in the Draft Critique forum. The second team that gets sent in is the team that will be written about here, and these tales will be sued to better describe their friendly relationship. This first tale in particular will describe why they are the way they are, and why they do what they do. It will describe their relationship and their drive.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I'd like to think it's unique and interesting because I will be using it, and subsequent tales, to tie all of my in-universe work together. I don't know how original this is, but I hope to add unique spins on the way character and plot development occurs.

Additional Notes: I wouldn't mind ideas on how to improve uniqueness and originality. And please, be brutally honest. If there's something you don't like, or something you do like, I'd greatly appreciate knowing what and why. Thank you in advance!

Footnotes
1. to be used for subsequent tales involving the team.

item.title: Any improvements?
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Item #: SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Keter Class

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is to be kept in a 50ft x 50ft Titanium room designed to look like a grazing field. The room is big enough to suit SCP-XXXX running needs. Steel shackles are to be locked to SCP-XXXX hind legs to at least slow it down. Reinforced sliding steel doors are locked in place when SCP-XXXX goes on its rampage. Two foundation agents who have taken courses on exorcism and have been dispatched by their teacher are to be kept at SCP-XXXX's containment cell at all times.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a male horse who has the ability to open a pocket dimension inside its underbelly. SCP-XXXX is normally friendly and isn't easily agitated. due to the side affects of the pocket dimension, It will go on a rampage once a week. This rampage usually lasts 1-2 hours. During the rampage, The pocket dimension opens and disembodied arms and hands burst from SCP-XXXX. Before recovery, these arms pillaged villages in Greece while SCP-XXXX is on its rampage. The foundation members managing SCP-XXXX's containment cell have given it the nickname, Trojan horse.

SCP-XXXX was discovered in [REDACTED], Greece on a farm where it was in is docile state. There had be a number of reports that week of a number of raids and pillages at neighboring villages. Later that week while field agents where following SCP-XXXX, They encountered it having its rampage. The pillage resulted in 10 civilians casualties and 2 agent casualties. The first recorded rampage the foundation had of SCP-XXXX lasted 1 hour. SCP-XXXX was recovered /9/10/2016/. Amnestics were given to all the involved villages.

item.title: Re: After Hours
item.content:encoded:
I'm willing to give a greenlight for this concept. I'd like to highlight a few things that are important.

The audio logs will explore the relationship between the two members of After Hours, developing their characters and showing their love for their work. In the end, it's revealed that the anomaly is a time capsule of some sort, meant to store the greatest moments of their lives.

This will be the crux of your story. You have to convey this clearly or else this article will have trouble gaining ground with a reader. Without this, you just have a ghost nightclub, which, don't get me wrong I like, would need a different tone, probably comedic, to work. With the more emotional side here, which once again is what your article should stand on, you need to give us characters that we can connect with.

Two people's love for music and each other is detailed as a faint memory through an eternal party. The anomaly is their happy ending- getting to perform for their fans and themselves until the end of time. It's an homage to parties and the love of musical expression that takes the reader on an emotional ride.

I believe this will do a suitable job of conveying the themes you're going for. Just be sure that the memory aspect is explored along with concluding with the end of time bit.

Overall, I see this succeeding, good luck!

item.title: Author's Post
item.content:encoded:
"The Circle rules your life."

This started out as me wanting to explore how modern people are like ants and from there it turned into a full blown meta-commentary on society and the Foundation.

TL;DR: We live in a society.

+ Here be spoilers
- Spoiled

The anomaly isn't just the pheromone. It's everything related to the Spiral. The essence of the spiral is cognitohazardous and spontaneous. There's no unknowable eldritch horror, no malicious Foundation secret, nothing that goes bump in the night and hides under your bed.

It just exists because it does and those are the most horrifying things to me.

The Foundation's pursuit of knowledge and answers, their insatiable desire to know everything is absolutely futile here. In fact, it is straight up detrimental to them because everything becomes a spiral, sooner or later.
